QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_52

question.text: A Leptokurtic distribution is characterized by:

answer.text: Kurtosis > 3, fatter tails, higher peak compared to normal

explanation.text: The Logic: Leptokurtic distributions have kurtosis higher than 3, equivalent to positive excess kurtosis. Their fatter tails and higher peak relative to the normal distribution indicate more outliers and inconsistent performance risk. The Trap: Platykurtic distributions have kurtosis less than 3, symmetry is a separate property, and saying there are no outliers contradicts the very fat-tail feature that defines leptokurtosis. Note: Per workbook pages 220-221 and sample question page 237.
